title: SE Enablement: Competitive Messaging & Demo Practice
next_steps: Record and upload demo clip of latency/batching slide (Liam) by 2027-09-24
Schedule 1:1 practice session for new AEs (Jamila) week of 2027-09-27
Update FAQ for dedicated vs hosted talking points (Maya) by 2027-09-28
summary: Internal SE enablement session focused on messaging for Dedicated vs Hosted, competitive positioning vs OpenAI/Anthropic, and live demo practice with common objection handling. Practice included a canary demo scenario, quick Q&A on security posture, and alignment on next steps to produce shareable enablement assets.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted: when to recommend which
Demo walkthrough: latency benchmarking, KV cache example, cost controls
Objection handling: SSO/KMS/SOC2, on-prem constraints, unit economics
transcript: 00:00 Maya Patel: ok everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a sec, uh this is the enablement on competitive messaging and demo practice. 00:12 Liam O'Connor: hey all, Liam here, i'll run the demo and Sophie will cover the battlecards, um quick note recording is on. 00:20 Sophie Nguyen: hi folks, I posted the slides and the battlecard link in the chat — deck link: https://redwood.internal/enablement/se/battlecard 00:32 Jamila Ford: got it, thanks. 00:35 Carlos Reyes: quick ask — target audience for the messaging, is it platform teams or product engineers? 00:42 Maya Patel: mostly platform teams, but hey we want the one-pager for product engineers too, so two layers of messaging. 00:51 Ethan Brooks: can we have a short elevator pitch for dedicated capacity? people always get lost in the details. 00:58 Maya Patel: yes, two-liner: "Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation — you buy reserved capacity for consistent QPS and isolation of data" — follow with a cost-to-value example. 01:12 Priya Shah: when customers ask about latency vs cost tradeoff, are we still pushing smart batching + prefix caching as the first lever? 01:21 Liam O'Connor: absolutely. show them that batching reduces per-token cost and KV cache reduces repeated prefix compute. demo will show a 30% cost drop in a common chat loop. 01:35 Sophie Nguyen: competitor note: OpenAI focuses on simplicity and model freshness, Anthropic on safety + system message support, Cohere is strong on embeddings cost, Vertex ties to cloud infra — we call out where Redwood beats them: serving economics and ops controls. 01:54 Jamila Ford: should SEs bring up SOC2 or wait until security asks? 02:01 Maya Patel: bring it up proactively — many buyers expect SOC2 and SSO. say "we're SOC 2 compliant, support SSO/SAML, KMS for customer-managed keys" and have the security whitepaper link ready. 02:16 Carlos Reyes: on private deployments, customers ask about air-gapped installs, what's the canned answer? 02:23 Liam O'Connor: "we offer Private (VPC or on-prem) with optional on-prem package for regulated workloads; we can integrate with your KMS/HSM and provide audit logs" — mention tailoring for large accounts. 02:38 Ethan Brooks: demo time? 02:41 Liam O'Connor: yep i'll share screen — show simple chat scenario first, then show dedicated config and time-to-first-byte comparisons. 02:50 [screen share starts] 02:58 Liam O'Connor: ok starting the chat loop with a 1024 token context — note the warm vs cold run, i'll show KV cache turned off first. 03:10 Maya Patel: call out the numbers, say "cold latency 420ms, warm 110ms" 03:16 Liam O'Connor: reading numbers... cold about four twenty, warm one ten. transcription: numbers may vary. 03:24 Priya Shah: you should translate that into user impact — e.g., interactive agent feels snappier, fewer dropped requests. 03:31 Sophie Nguyen: also bring up cost per 1k tokens — show that with batching we go from $0.12 to $0.08 per 1k tokens in this scenario. 03:42 Liam O'Connor: switching to dedicated pool view, here's the throughput graph, we can pin to model v1.3 and set autoscale policies. 03:50 Carlos Reyes: do we have a quick phrase for model rollouts and fallbacks? 03:54 Maya Patel: yes: "we support canary rollouts with automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants for reliability under load". 04:05 Jamila Ford: objection practice — i'll play a buyer: "We already use OpenAI for prototyping, why switch?" 04:12 Maya Patel: good, Liam take this. 04:14 Liam O'Connor (as buyer): well, we like OpenAI for model quality but we're concerned about cost and control at scale. 04:21 Liam O'Connor: response: "OpenAI is great for prototyping; for production we recommend Redwood when teams need predictable unit economics, private deployment options, and stronger observability/rollouts — it's not an either/or, it's about having the right tool for production." 04:40 Ethan Brooks: what about hallucination risk, how do we talk about quality monitoring? 04:45 Sophie Nguyen: say we provide quality monitoring, prompt regression alerts, and can tie evals to your test prompts — we also recommend model selection and quantization guidance to keep quality predictable. 04:58 Maya Patel: can we role-play procurement? buyer: "We have strict data residency — can Redwood do region locking?" 05:06 Liam O'Connor: reply: "yes, we can pin deployments to regions and support customer-managed networking for Private; discuss compliance packages for audit traces." 05:20 Sophie Nguyen: small note: avoid overclaiming on certs — if they push ISO or FedRAMP, route to Security for timelines. 05:30 [brief cross-talk] 05:36 Jamila Ford: demo redo — focus on the story: problem statement, config choice, live metric, and customer outcome. 05:45 Liam O'Connor: ok running again, this time show the batching toggle and the KV cache effect on repeated queries. 05:58 Liam O'Connor: batching on — throughput up, cost per token down, latency slightly higher for single reqs but overall better unit economics. 06:10 Maya Patel: call out tradeoff language: "optimize for unit economics vs latency SLO; we can tune batching and cache per route". 06:22 Carlos Reyes: competitor angle — customers will ask about model freshness and safety. quick line? 06:27 Sophie Nguyen: "we support curated model catalog with verified perf profiles and continuous safety tooling" — and point to verified benchmark deck. 06:38 Ethan Brooks: someone asked about autoscale cold start — do we have a standard answer? 06:44 Liam O'Connor: yes: "we reduce cold starts with warm pools and smart routing; Dedicated offers much lower TTFB under steady QPS". 06:55 Priya Shah: i raised a point earlier about KV cache naming — sometimes we call it 'prefix cache' in docs, avoid confusing customers. 07:02 Maya Patel: good catch, make battlecard consistent: use 'prefix/KV cache (prefix cache is same as KV cache)' and include a one-line explainer. 07:12 [15 second pause, notes being typed] 07:28 Jamila Ford: final Q&A — any sticky points SEs want help scripting? 07:34 Ethan Brooks: how to handle pricing asks when customer pushes for line-item unit cost? 07:39 Maya Patel: give a ballpark but avoid firm quote — say "we'll follow up with a tailored cost model after we understand load patterns" and then hand off to sales ops for formal quote. 07:52 Carlos Reyes: action: we'll iterate the one-pager and the demo clip. 07:58 Maya Patel: thanks everyone — recap: Sophie will share battlecard, Liam will cut demo clip, Jamila will set 1:1s, Maya will update FAQs. expect deliverables by end of week. 08:10 [meeting ends]
